summary: Full-flow staged-combustion methane/LOX engines for Super Heavy and Starship. Flight vehicles use Raptor 2 on early integrated flights; Raptor 3 cited for Starship V3 / recent flights per SpaceX updates.

super_heavy.note: Super Heavy uses 33 sea-level Raptors in the centre cluster (public Starship reference architecture).

starship.note: Ship: 3 centre sea-level Raptors + 3 Raptor Vacuum (RVac) in outer ring.

versions.name: Raptor 1
versions.thrust_note: SpaceX-published April 2024 comparison graphic (sea level / vacuum).
versions.chamber_pressure_bar: 250 (design target, not public sustained flight value)

versions.name: Raptor 2
versions.status: used on integrated flight tests through Block 2 era
versions.chamber_pressure_note: Musk: Raptor 2 operates routinely at 300 bar main chamber pressure (Jan 2022).
versions.specific_impulse_vac_s: not public (single cited sea-level Isp 347 in SpaceX graphic)
versions.production_note: NSF reporting: at least 569 Raptor 2 engines produced by Aug 2024.

versions.name: Raptor 3
versions.status: flight engines on Starship V3 per SpaceX Starship update
versions.thrust_target_note: SpaceX 2024 target card 280 tf; May 2026 Starship V3 update cites 250 tf flight sea-level, 275 tf RVac.
versions.chamber_pressure_bar: 350 (test peak, May 2023); routine flight pressure not public

facilities.role: Raptor engine production and assembly (SpaceX factory)

facilities.role: Raptor development and acceptance testing (vertical test stands)

production_milestones.text: Musk stated SpaceX goal path toward building a Raptor about every 48 hours (aspirational cadence, not verified production log).
Public reporting: at least 569 Raptor 2 engines produced.
SpaceX published Raptor 3 target specs (280 tf, 350 s Isp, 1525 kg engine mass).
Starship V3 update: flight Raptor 3 at 250 tf (SL) and 275 tf (vacuum); ~1 t mass saving per engine vs Raptor 2 at vehicle level.

flight_engine_events.summary: Several of 33 booster engines shut down before/during ascent; staging not achieved.
One Raptor lost early on ascent; mission still met splashdown goals.
Ship engines shut down early (propellant leak); booster catch succeeded.
Booster lost one engine on ascent; engine-out demonstration to Gulf splashdown.
Booster lost one outboard engine on ascent; 20 of 33 failed to relight on boostback.
One ship engine shut down on ascent; orbital insertion and payload deploy proceeded.
